newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER - NO JOHANSSON INVESTIGATION, SAYS UEFA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - NO JOHANSSON INVESTIGATION, SAYS UEFA.

text.p: General secretary Gerhard Aigner said on Monday that UEFA would not be conducting an internal inquiry into alleged racist remarks made by president Lennart Johansson.
The head of European soccer's governing body, Johansson is alleged to have made comments, including the word blackies, about a recent trip to South Africa, triggering a storm of criticism.

Aigner, arriving in Amsterdam for a UEFA congress, not only denied reports of an internal investigation but rushed to Johansson's defence saying: "We all know about the integrity of Lennart Johansson.
He added: "There's nothing to investigate. One has to wonder how these reports are being made up."

Johansson has kept a low profile since his comments first appeared in a Swedish newspaper last week but the 67-year-old is expected to make an appearance at the week-long meetings starting on Tuesday.
A FIFA vice-president, Johansson has apologised for the remarks. He said he could not recall using the term "blackie" but could not exclude it.
"I am not a racist. I apologise to anyone who interpreted it (the interview) as if I was one," he added.
